title: AIDA research file
description: One file per search, at <task folder>/research/<search>.json (ideal/research.md, 'What research writes'). Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. This is the only part a script reads; <search>.md, rendered from it by research-render.sh, is for the design stage to read and no script parses it. A field present in a real research file but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field alignment.json, task.json and project.json all carry. A repair reads format-changes.md by this number and applies the change that matches, instead of guessing the old shape from what the file happens to contain. Bumped only when a later change to this schema says so, never for a value change inside an unchanged shape. Read from the file directly: this file carries no frontmatter fence, so schemaVersion sits at the file's own top level.

search.description: The name of the search this file records, for example "prior-art-internal" or "guides-and-recipes". Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, since this value doubles as the file's own basename: <search>.md. There is no fixed roster of search names (ideal/research.md, 'How many run is set by what the criteria need, not by a standing roster'); a name is chosen when the search is dispatched and never reused for a different subject within the same task.

searchedFor.description: The words this search actually searched for, as words, never prose about how it searched (ideal/research.md, 'Each agent gets a narrow brief'). It is what bounds every negative result in this file: foundations.md says a bounded search proves nothing outside its bounds, and without this field "looked and found nothing" states no bound at all, so a later stage cannot tell a subject that was searched and came back empty from one nobody searched. The design stage reads it to decide what it must look up itself, since it names things to use that did not exist as decisions when research ran. Set by the `record` action on every call for a search, and the same value each time: a second value for one search is refused rather than merged, because the search is the unit and a broadened search is a new search with its own name.

findings.description: What this search turned up, in the order it was recorded. A search that found nothing still holds one finding whose text says so (ideal/research.md, "'Looked and found nothing' is a finding"), because silence and a negative result look identical from outside, and only the recorded negative tells the design stage it is safe to decide without looking again.

text.description: What was found, or that nothing was, in plain words. Never the model's recall: a claim with no source behind it is not a finding (ideal/research.md, 'Research means looking, never recalling'). For a guide or a recipe, this names it and says which of the three classes it is; research identifies it without reading it, so this is a pointer for the design stage, not a summary of its content.

source.description: Where this was found: a file path inside the project, a package registry entry, a guide's or a recipe's own location, or a URL. This is also the link the design stage opens, since research names what it found without reading it (ideal/research.md, 'Identify a guide, do not read it').

lookedAt.description: The UTC date this finding was looked at, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script at the moment the finding is recorded, not typed by hand, so a source that was searched and came back empty stays dated distinctly from one nobody has searched yet (ideal/research.md, 'Grounding a claim about a mechanism').

criteriaServed.description: The acceptance criterion ids, minted by scope in alignment.json, that this finding serves. Empty is allowed and is itself meaningful: a finding with no criterion is work nobody asked for, and the both-directions check reports it rather than the schema refusing to record it (ideal/research.md, 'What a finding holds'). Holds ids, never criterion text, so rewording a criterion later costs nothing here.
